body:
## Summary
The Analyze form decides where a dropped file goes by which DOM node caught the event. That decision is spread over one window listener inside the CV column, three per-zone onDrop handlers, a DOM-attribute carve-out and a prop-order override. Four silent losses fall out of it. Replace it with one pure router: zones declare an id (cv, jd, company), one window listener hosted by the form resolves the id and plans the whole drop, and every file that does not go in is named with a reason.

## Description
Today: (1) a file dropped on the attached JD or company card is swallowed, because the card is marked owned but has no handler and the window catch skips owned targets. (2) A multi-file drop on the JD or company zone keeps the first file and loses the rest. (3) A CV batch stops at the first invalid file, so valid files after it are never tried. (4) 'Page' can only mean 'CV', because the page catch belongs to the CV column. Behind those sit two drop dispatchers per event, coordinated by `data-file-dropzone` and by spread order in AnalyzeProfileInput.tsx:179-188, plus an overlay threaded through the list as props.

The move: `data-file-dropzone` carries a zone id from one closed vocabulary (`DROP_ZONES = ['cv','jd','company'] as const`, derived union, runtime guard: the house pattern). `analyzeDropRouting.ts` gains `resolveDropZone(target)` and `planDrop(zone, files, snapshot)`. The plan runs `acceptUpload` per file, applies the CV cap from the snapshot, treats JD and company as single slots (a drop on a filled slot replaces it), and returns `{cv, jd, company, refused[]}`. AnalyzeForm hosts the one `useGlobalFileDrag` and applies the plan through the setters it already holds: addCvFile, setJobDescriptionFile + setSelectedJdSlug(null), setCompanyFile. Refusals render once in a form-level status line. Zone components keep only the counted highlight. Their file pickers call the same `onIntake(zone, files)`, so a click and a drop can no longer diverge. `useFileAccept` retires because its gate now lives in the plan. The hook keeps the dedupe and the race-safe cap re-check, so that authority does not move.

This card deliberately does not touch useAnalyzeCvFiles.ts, useAnalyzeForm.ts, AnalyzeTab.tsx or AnalyzeApi.ts. Those files are in challenge-r02's analyze-engine write sets and are being built now.

## Flow
1. The recruiter drops 3 files anywhere on the form. The one window listener calls resolveDropZone(event.target), which returns 'page', then planDrop('page', files, snapshot).
2. The plan runs: two CVs go in and the third is refused for 'cap'. AnalyzeForm commits the CVs through addCvFile, and the status line reads 'third.pdf was not added: you can attach up to 3 CV variants'.
3. The recruiter drops a new JD onto the attached JD card. The zone resolves to 'jd' and the plan returns replaces:true. setJobDescriptionFile runs and the saved-JD slug detaches, the same rule the picker follows.
4. A drop on the JD zone with two files: the first becomes the JD and the second is refused with 'single-slot'.

## Expected impact
Four silent file losses become either a correct commit or a named refusal. Intake goes from two dispatchers and one carve-out attribute to one listener and one pure decision that node:test can cover. A later mode (a mixed-drop sort tray, apply-page reuse) then has one seam to extend instead of five.

## Evaluation
Claim: every Analyze drop resolves through one pure zone-id router, and no dropped file is lost without a named reason.
Before: 0 of 8 acceptance cases pass (resolveDropZone and planDrop do not exist; the window listener lives in AnalyzeProfileInput and counts inline).
After: 8 of 8.
Method: gate - node:test over analyzeDropRouting.test.ts (pure cases 1-7) plus the source guard (case 8) in analyzeFileIntakeGate.test.ts; tsc, lint, i18n:check.
Result: pending build.
Gate: architecture

title: Preflight what the engine can read: per-CV text check and a blind-mode guard
acceptance: readabilityFromExtract({ok:true, charCount:0, pageCount:2}) -> {kind:'no-text', pages:2}; ({ok:true, charCount:4120, pageCount:2}) -> {kind:'readable', chars:4120, pages:2}

readabilityFromExtract({ok:false, status:429}), ({ok:false, status:504}) and a network throw -> {kind:'unchecked'}; ({ok:false, status:400, code:'EXTRACT_TEXT_UNREADABLE'}) -> {kind:'unreadable'}
preflightVerdict({blind:false, cvs:[no-text]}) -> {blockRun:false, notes:[{cv:0, kind:'model-read'}]}: without blind the model reads the file itself, so the run proceeds with an honest note
preflightVerdict({blind:true, cvs:[unchecked]}) -> {blockRun:false}: an unknown never blocks a run (degrade, never block)

app/features/tools/analyze/AnalyzeFormFooter.tsx:65-71 and :95 - the blind checkbox and the Analyze button sit together in the footer, and the button's disabled condition knows nothing about readability

rollback: Purely additive client code: the preflight module, hook and strip are new files, the footer gains one component and one extra disabled term, and no route, schema or engine code changes. Reverting the commits restores today's footer, and the catalogs lose only the new analyze.preflight* keys.
runner_up: A mixed-drop sort tray: drop a JD and two CVs anywhere and confirm a per-file destination chip (CV / JD / company) pre-guessed from the filename before anything commits. Traded away because it rides on slot A's router and its guess is weaker evidence than a measured extract.
body:
## Summary
A recruiter attaches a scanned CV, ticks Blind and presses Analyze. The run uploads, queues and extracts, then fails with engine English telling them to turn Blind off. In a 3-variant compare the scanned variant quietly falls out after the other two engine calls have spent. The same scan used as a JD file quietly yields a JD-blind score. The app can know all of this before the click: /api/extract-text already returns charCount and pageCount. Preflight every attached file, show what the engine will read in a strip above the Analyze button, and turn the doomed combination (blind plus a CV with no text layer) into a stated block with one-click remedies.

## Description
`analyzeCvReadability.ts` is pure and holds the bands and the verdict. `readabilityFromExtract` maps an extract answer to readable, thin, no-text, unreadable or unchecked. `preflightVerdict({blind, cvs, jd, jdTextTyped})` returns blockRun, per-file notes and remedies. The rules follow the blind-screening standard (fail-closed-on-an-unmaskable-document): refuse only when the document cannot be masked at all, never on an unknown, and never strand the run without a remedy. `useAnalyzeReadability(cvFiles, jdFile)` measures each file once: .txt and .md locally via file.text(), PDF and DOCX through /api/extract-text, cached by cvVariantHash, with 429, 504 and network errors mapped to 'unchecked'. `AnalyzeReadabilityStrip` renders one row per variant plus the JD file, for example 'Variant A · 2 pages · 4,120 chars', 'Variant B · no text layer: blind screening cannot redact it' or 'JD file · no readable text: the match will run without it'. It also renders the remedies as buttons: 'Run without blind' (setBlind(false)) and 'Remove variant B' (handlers.removeCvFile(1)). AnalyzeFormFooter mounts the strip and adds `verdict.blockRun` to the button's disabled condition. Both setters are already on `state`. The server-side fail-closed stays exactly as it is, so the preflight is an earlier, kinder copy of a refusal the engine still enforces. It is not a new gate.

The write set avoids useAnalyzeForm.ts, useAnalyzeCvFiles.ts, AnalyzeTab.tsx and AnalyzeApi.ts, which challenge-r02's analyze-engine cards are building now. The hook reads `state.inputs` and makes its own fetch, and does not extend extractFileText.

## Flow
1. The recruiter drops cv-scan.pdf and cv-2024.docx. The strip shows both as 'checking…' and then 'no text layer' and '3 pages · 5,210 chars'.
2. They tick Blind. The strip turns the scan row into a coral block ('Blind screening cannot redact a document with no text'), the Analyze button disables with that reason, and two buttons appear: Run without blind, and Remove variant A.
3. They click Remove variant A. The verdict clears, and a blind single-CV run proceeds on the readable file.
4. Without Blind, the scan row stays an amber note ('the model will read the file directly') and nothing blocks.
5. A scanned JD PDF plus pasted JD text gives the note 'the attached JD file has no readable text and will be used instead of your pasted text; remove the file to use the text'.

## Expected impact
The one blind-mode failure the engine can only report after the fact becomes a decision the recruiter makes before spending. A best-of-N compare no longer shrinks silently. A JD-blind score from an empty JD file stops passing as a real match. The extract counts built in eceb983e9 finally reach a caller that warns.

## Evaluation
Claim: before submit, Analyze reports what the engine can read of every attached file and blocks only the blind plus no-text combination, with a remedy.
Before: 0 of 8 acceptance cases pass (no readability module exists; the counts are unread).
After: 8 of 8.
Method: gate - node:test over analyzeCvReadability.test.ts (cases 1-8, the fetch injected); tsc, lint, i18n:check, design:check for the strip's amber/coral tokens.
Result: pending build.
Gate: none
